```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, cache = FALSE, error = FALSE)
source("_common/sim_report.R")
```

Summary of the completed six-experiment refresh, matching the updated
`stage1_main.html` reports. Numerical values are read from the same saved
100-replication results used by those HTML files, before display rounding.
No models are fitted while generating this summary. For the DGP definitions,
see [the simulation overview](README.md).

## What "phase 1 → phase 2" means

Every simulation fits the *same* entry-time-aware model (`cox_lt`/`rsf_lt`) on
the *same* replication twice:

- **Phase 1**: that model is given an entry vector of all zeros — i.e.
  "pretend nothing is truncated."
- **Phase 2**: that same model is given the real, observed entry times.

Each comparison is **paired within a model family**: the same observed
sample, seeds, and hyperparameters, with entry information changed at fitting.
Both phases use left-truncated data; setting entry to zero does not recover
subjects excluded before observation. Ordinary and zero-entry fits were also
fitted independently to check their survival-curve agreement in every replication.

```{r load}
sims <- c(
  "01" = "01_cox_random_forerst_lt",
  "02" = "02_flexihaz_gompertz_lt",
  "03" = "03_rist_scenario1_lt",
  "04" = "04_rist_scenario2_lt",
  "05" = "05_rist_scenario3_lt",
  "06" = "06_rist_scenario4_lt"
)
dgp_label <- c(
  "01" = "Cox PH (exactly Cox)",
  "02" = "Gompertz-shape (PH violation)",
  "03" = "RIST Sc.1 (exactly Cox)",
  "04" = "RIST Sc.2 (nonlinear link)",
  "05" = "RIST Sc.3 (Gamma, PH violation)",
  "06" = "RIST Sc.4 (Lognormal, PH violation)"
)
metrics <- c(overall = "MAD", cindex = "C-idx", brier = "CRPS", auc = "AUC err")
## Pin the completed run used for the current HTML reports and thesis.
## The original per-scenario RDS files are historical; do not silently use them.
results_run <- file.path("reruns", "2026-11-06-1802cc3")
run_manifest <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(results_run, "manifest.json"),
                                    simplifyVector = TRUE)
stopifnot(run_manifest$state == "complete")
expected_provenance <- readRDS(file.path(results_run, "package-provenance.rds"))

res_list <- lapply(sims, function(d) {
  result <- readRDS(file.path(results_run, "results", d, "results_phases.rds"))
  stopifnot(result$n_rep == run_manifest$n_rep,
            result$m_test == run_manifest$test_subjects_per_replication,
            identical(result$package_provenance, expected_provenance),
            identical(result$run_provenance$source_commit, run_manifest$source_commit),
            all(result$noop$rsf == 0), all(result$noop$cox < 1e-8))
  for (field in names(metrics)) {
    stopifnot(!is.null(result[[field]]),
              nrow(result[[field]]) == result$n_rep,
              all(is.finite(as.matrix(result[[field]]))))
  }
  result
})
names(res_list) <- names(sims)

## A completed run must supply every declared metric; missing fields stop rendering.
has_auc <- "auc" %in% names(metrics)

## % improvement from phase 1 -> phase 2, lower-is-better for every metric
## here, so positive = entry time helped.
pct_improve <- function(res, field, family) {
  pt  <- phase_table(res, field = field)
  row <- pt[pt$variant == "left-truncation" & pt$family == family, ]
  (row$phase1 - row$phase2) / row$phase1 * 100
}

summary_tbl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sims), function(nm) {
  res <- res_list[[nm]]
  row <- c(`#` = nm, DGP = dgp_label[[nm]])
  for (f in names(metrics)) {
    row[paste0(metrics[[f]], " Cox")] <-
      sprintf("%.2f%%", pct_improve(res, f, "Cox"))
    row[paste0(metrics[[f]], " RSF")] <-
      sprintf("%.2f%%", pct_improve(res, f, "RSF"))
  }
  row
}))

## Read the replication count back off the saved results rather than
## hardcoding it, so this line can never go stale against the numbers it
## describes -- same rule as everything else in this file.
n_rep_all  <- vapply(res_list, function(r) as.integer(r$n_rep),  integer(1))
m_test_all <- vapply(res_list, function(r) as.integer(r$m_test), integer(1))
zero_rsf <- max(vapply(res_list, function(r) max(r$noop$rsf), numeric(1)))
zero_cox <- max(vapply(res_list, function(r) max(r$noop$cox), numeric(1)))
scenario_reports <- data.frame(
  Scenario = names(sims), DGP = unname(dgp_label),
  Report = if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
    sprintf('<a href="%s/stage1_main.html">HTML</a>', unname(sims))
  } else {
    paste0("[HTML](", unname(sims), "/stage1_main.html)")
  }
)
fmt_range <- function(v) if (length(unique(v)) == 1) as.character(v[1]) else
  paste0(min(v), "-", max(v), " (varies by sim)")
```

> **Run size:** `r fmt_range(n_rep_all)` replications per experiment,
> **`r sum(n_rep_all)` total**, with `r fmt_range(m_test_all)` population test
> covariates per replication. Each fit uses
> `r run_manifest$training_subjects_per_replication` retained training subjects
> and `r run_manifest$trees_per_forest` trees.
>
> **Provenance:** package/source commit
> `r substr(run_manifest$source_commit, 1, 7)`, completed
> `r substr(run_manifest$completed_utc, 1, 10)`.
> All completed results passed independent zero-entry checks: maximum RSF
> survival-curve difference `r zero_rsf`, maximum Cox difference
> `r format(zero_cox, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)`.

The summary reads only this completed, fingerprinted run. Historical saved
results and earlier HTML copies are preserved under its source archive.
Differences from historical numbers combine our fixes and upstream changes;
they do not isolate the effect of an individual fix.

Every column is **% improvement from supplying the real entry time**
(`(phase1 - phase2) / phase1 * 100`), computed on each metric's *error*
scale. So for every column alike, positive = entry time helped, negative =
it made that arm/metric worse.

MAD and Brier are lower-is-better as they stand. The two ranking metrics are
converted to errors first so they sit on that same scale: the C-index column
is computed on `1 - C`, and the AUC column on `1 - AUC`. Read an AUC entry
of `2.9%` as *"the AUC error shrank by 2.9%"* — not as an AUC rising by 2.9
points.

```{r table}
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(summary_tbl, row.names = FALSE))
```

Curve accuracy improves in all six scenarios for both model families.
The concordance result is mixed: RSF concordance error increases in Scenarios
1–3; the small changes in Scenarios 3–4 have paired descriptive intervals
that include zero. In Scenario 2, the RSF concordance deterioration occurs
in every replication. A smaller ranking change does not imply a smaller
survival-curve improvement.

MAD compares unconditioned predictions with source-population survival truth
on independent test covariates. Concordance, CRPS, and AUC use training
outcomes: RSF contributes OOB curves, whereas Cox contributes in-sample curves.
Brier/CRPS and AUC describe entered subjects using pooled delayed-entry
Kaplan–Meier censoring weights. These scores assess different targets, and the
pooled model's common-censoring-hazard assumption is stronger than conditional
independence given covariates and entry. The AUC construction is our project
extension, rather than an estimator prescribed by the professor's outline.

CRPS is the **unnormalized time integral** of the Brier curve; its raw values
depend on the scenario's evaluation horizon. Absolute paired phase shifts,
descriptive intervals, and replication counts are in
[the numerical summary](reruns/2026-11-06-1802cc3/summary.csv).
There, `paired_shift` is phase 2 minus phase 1 (negative favors entry-aware
fitting); the percentage-reduction table above uses the opposite direction
so positive means improvement.

## By metric

```{r plot-setup}
COL_COX  <- "#e6550d"   # same pair used throughout sim_report.R's own plots
COL_RSF  <- "#31a354"
COL_GRID <- "grey85"
COL_REF  <- "grey60"

pct_matrix <- function(field) {
  m <- t(vapply(names(sims), function(nm) {
    res <- res_list[[nm]]
    c(Cox = pct_improve(res, field, "Cox"),
      RSF = pct_improve(res, field, "RSF"))
  }, numeric(2)))
  rownames(m) <- names(sims)
  m
}

plot_metric_bars <- function(field, label) {
  m <- pct_matrix(field)
  ylim <- range(c(0, m), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.15
  barplot(t(m), beside = TRUE, col = c(COL_COX, COL_RSF), border = NA,
          ylim = ylim, las = 1, ylab = "% improvement (phase 1 -> phase 2)",
          main = label, names.arg = rownames(m), cex.names = 0.9)
  abline(h = 0, col = COL_REF, lwd = 1.5)
  grid(nx = NA, ny = NULL, col = COL_GRID, lty = 1)
  box(col = COL_GRID)
  legend("topright", legend = c("Cox", "RSF"), fill = c(COL_COX, COL_RSF),
         border = NA, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
}

## Which arm/metric combinations actually went backwards, read off the data
## rather than asserted in prose -- so this sentence cannot go stale against
## the numbers it describes when the run size changes.
neg_cells <- unlist(lapply(names(metrics), function(f) {
  m  <- pct_matrix(f)
  ix <- which(m < 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
  if (!nrow(ix)) NULL else sprintf("%s %s", metrics[[f]], colnames(m)[ix[, "col"]])
}))
neg_txt <- if (!length(neg_cells)) "no arm/metric in this run" else
  knitr::combine_words(sort(unique(neg_cells)))
```

Same numbers as the table above, as `r length(metrics)` small multiples (one
axis each — `r knitr::combine_words(unname(metrics))` live on very different
scales, so one shared axis would be misleading). The zero line is the
reference: bars crossing below it are where entry time made that arm/metric
*worse* — in this run, `r neg_txt`.

```{r plot-mad, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
plot_metric_bars("overall", "MAD vs true S")
```

```{r plot-cindex, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
plot_metric_bars("cindex", "Concordance error (1-C)")
```

```{r plot-brier, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
plot_metric_bars("brier", "Integrated Brier / CRPS")
```

```{r plot-auc, fig.width=7, fig.height=4, eval=has_auc}
plot_metric_bars("auc", "Time-averaged AUC error")
```

## Detailed reports

```{r report-links}
knitr::kable(scenario_reports, escape = !knitr::is_html_output())
```

These HTML reports use the same completed result objects as this summary.
The result objects are stored under
`reruns/2026-11-06-1802cc3/results/<scenario>/results_phases.rds`.
Each report also shows AUC over time; a single time average can flatten
differences concentrated in one interval of follow-up.
The [Hebrew summary](../docs/summary_hebrew.md) gives a short explanation
of the results and remaining scope.
